subject: Difference in detection probabilites in occu and pcount question

messages.author: ff8b92e3478bd700
messages.subject: Difference in detection probabilites in occu and pcount question
parts:
Hello group,

I am using a single season data set that includes 5 different focal species. I am looking at each species and using 2 obsCovs (date and time) and 5 siteCovs (habitat measurements).
I am analyzing my data using occu and pcount to get detection probabilities, occupancy, and abundance estimates.  My main issue is the differences in prob. of detection between pcount and occu. For example when backtransforming my null models, prob of detection using occu for spp.1 is 0.291+/-0.04 but when using pcount, detection estimates are 0.129 +/-0.05. I've graphed detection probabilities over time and date using my occu results but when I went to model/graph it with pcount it is much different (as expected from my output). I'm wondering which would be the appropriate one to use/report and also, why would they be so different?

Thank you in advance!

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Difference in detection probabilites in occu and pcount question
parts:
hi Nicole,
 the pcount() model, i.e., the N-mixture model, has a detection probability parameter that is "the probability of detecting an INDIVIDUAL" where as the occupancy model is the "probability of detecting the SPECIES" 
 so the former is individual-level and the latter is species level.
regards
andy

messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Difference in detection probabilites in occu and pcount question
parts:
HI Nicole,

 

The detection parameters in these two different types of model have different interpretations.

In pcount, I believe you are estimating the probability of detecting an _individual_ if its there, whereas in occu, you are estimating the probability of detecting the species if it’s there (at least 1 individual, or sign, or whatever). So, you would expect these values to be different, although they can be somewhat related.

 

Its appropriate to use both, but in context of course.

 

Chris

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Re: Difference in detection probabilites in occu and pcount question
parts:
Hi Nicole,

and the two detection probs are related like the following:

P* = 1 - (1-p)^N,

where P* is the occupancy detection probability: the prob to detect at least one of the N individuals present. That is equal to 1 minus the prob to detect none of the N of them.

Hence, whenever there are more than 1 ind. per site, the Nmix detection prob will be less than the occu detection prob.

Regards  -- Marc
